landmarks.name: Golden Gate Bridge
landmarks.blurb: Opened 1937, painted International Orange; its 227 m towers held the world record span for 27 years.

landmarks.name: Bay Bridge (West Span)
landmarks.blurb: Twin suspension spans joined by a massive central anchorage, linking SF to Yerba Buena Island since 1936.

landmarks.name: Transamerica Pyramid
landmarks.blurb: The 260 m pyramid of 1972 - once hated, now the icon of the Financial District skyline.

landmarks.name: Salesforce Tower
landmarks.blurb: At 326 m the tallest tower in San Francisco; its crown is an LED art screen at night.

landmarks.name: Coit Tower
landmarks.blurb: A 64 m fluted concrete column atop Telegraph Hill (1933), lined with WPA-era murals.

landmarks.name: Ferry Building
landmarks.blurb: The 1898 Beaux-Arts terminal with its 75 m clock tower, now a beloved food hall.

landmarks.name: Palace of Fine Arts
landmarks.blurb: A Roman-ruin rotunda built for the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition, mirrored in its lagoon.

landmarks.name: San Francisco City Hall
landmarks.blurb: Beaux-Arts landmark of 1915 whose gilded dome rises taller than the US Capitol.

landmarks.name: Alcatraz Island
landmarks.blurb: "The Rock": federal penitentiary 1934-1963, with the oldest lighthouse on the West Coast.

landmarks.name: Pier 39
landmarks.blurb: Waterfront shopping pier famous for the sea lions that moved in after the 1989 earthquake.

landmarks.name: Painted Ladies
landmarks.blurb: The row of pastel Victorians on Alamo Square - "Postcard Row" - built 1892-1896.

landmarks.name: Oracle Park
landmarks.blurb: Waterfront ballpark of the Giants; home runs over right field splash into McCovey Cove.

landmarks.name: Ghirardelli Square
landmarks.blurb: Chocolate factory turned plaza; its glowing rooftop sign has lit the Wharf since 1923.

landmarks.name: Chinatown Dragon Gate
landmarks.blurb: The 1970 gateway at Grant & Bush, entrance to the oldest Chinatown in North America.

landmarks.name: Lombard Street
landmarks.blurb: "The crookedest street in the world": eight hairpins down one brick-paved block of Russian Hill.

landmarks.name: Fort Point
landmarks.blurb: Civil War-era brick fort tucked under the southern arch of the Golden Gate Bridge.

tracks.name: Embarcadero Sprint
tracks.description: Flat-out along the waterfront: Jefferson St past Pier 39, down The Embarcadero's palm-lined boulevard, past the Ferry Building clock tower and the Bay Bridge to the ballpark.

tracks.name: Lombard Zigzag
tracks.description: Tight Russian Hill circuit: plunge down the eight hairpins of crooked Lombard Street, loop the flats by the bay and claw back up Hyde Street past the cable cars.

tracks.name: Golden Gate Run
tracks.area: Marina to the Golden Gate Bridge
tracks.description: From the Marina Green along Crissy Field and up through the Presidio, then onto the Golden Gate Bridge deck, 67 m above the water, and across past the north tower.

tracks.name: Nob Hill Jumps
tracks.description: Bullitt-style hill bombing: California Street over Nob Hill, then Jones and Taylor Streets where every cross street is a launch ramp.

tracks.name: Downtown Grand Prix
tracks.description: A street circuit between the skyscrapers: Market Street, Montgomery to the Transamerica Pyramid, Columbus Avenue, Broadway and back down The Embarcadero.

tracks.name: Painted Ladies Tour
tracks.area: Alamo Square, the Panhandle and Golden Gate Park
tracks.description: Past Postcard Row on Alamo Square, west along the Panhandle on Fell Street to the edge of Golden Gate Park and back on Oak Street.

tracks.name: Bay Bridge Run
tracks.area: Bay Bridge and Yerba Buena Island
tracks.description: From the Embarcadero under the bridge, up onto the Bay Bridge, through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel and down the east span to Oakland.
